key_insight: T2D-Bench tests whether LLM diabetes advice is not just fluent, but explicitly backed by graph-checkable evidence and guideline constraints.
clinical_relevance: This framework could help clinicians and developers identify unsupported omissions or unsafe lifestyle claims in type 2 diabetes AI outputs before they are used in practice.
method: Built a multi-layer knowledge graph combining UMLS, DrugBank, SIDER, ADA rules, and lifestyle-to-glycemia links
Evaluated LLM answers across 100 structured vignettes covering diagnosis, medication safety, and adversarial lifestyle conflicts
Applied an evidence gate and constrained revision to check and improve benchmark-defined compliance
evidence_signal: In 100 vignettes, baseline outputs failed evidence-path checks in 35% of GPT-4o-mini cases and 33% of GPT-4o cases.
watch_item: The benchmark focuses on graph-checkable evidence and may not capture all nuanced clinical judgment or real-world patient context.
paper_title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
